newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel seals houses of West Bank Palestinians.
newsitem.headline: Israel seals houses of West Bank Palestinians.

text.p: Israeli soldiers on Friday welded shut the homes of three suspected Moslem militants in the West Bank village of Sourif, igniting clashes with Palestinians, witnesses said.
They said Palestinian youths defied a curfew on Sourif and attacked soldiers with stones, who responded with rubber bullets and tear gas.

Witnesses said 12-year-old girl Mona al-Heeh was shot in the thigh, rupturing a vein. A medic stitched up the wound and rushed her to a hospital in near-by Hebron. Another 16-year-old boy was also wounded.

"Israel does not punish the real criminals or their families who carry out crimes against the Palestinian people," said the mother of one of the suspects, Sara Ahmed al-Qadi, 60, who owns one of the houses.
"They are just quick to punish us for fighting for our country," she said.

Israeli and Palestinian security forces have rounded up five Sourif residents suspected of belonging to a Hamas cell accused of killing 11 Israelis since early 1996, including Sergeant Sharon Edri, 19, who went missing last September.
Edri's body was found buried in a Sourif olive grove on Thursday.
A fifth member of the cell died last month when a bomb he carried into a Tel Aviv cafe exploded, killing him and three Israeli women. The army said it went off prematurely.

Many of Sourif's 13,000 Palestinians watched from their windows as Israeli soldiers ordered the families of Ibrahim Abdallah Ghneimat, 30, Jamal Abdel-Fattah al-Hour, 28, and Abdel-Rahman Ismael Ghneimat, 27, to remove their furniture from the houses.
Residents said soldiers also handed the owners demolition orders that give the families time to appeal to Israel's High Court.
Israel, using emergency regulations dating back to British rule over Palestine, routinely closes or destroys houses where Arabs suspected of carrying out attacks against Jews had lived.
Some women ululated in defiance as youths hurled stones at the soldiers who fixed metal sheets to the houses' windows and welded shut iron doors.
"I am proud that my son is a fighter for his country and for God. We will build a bigger and a better house," Qadi said defiantly.
Earlier in the day, Israeli soldiers shot and wounded more than 15 Palestinians during street battles with stone-throwing Arabs in Hebron.

Hebron, a flashpoint of Arab-Jewish violence, has been the scene of daily clashes since Tuesday when Jewish settlers shot dead a Palestinian shopkeeper near the al-Ibrahimi mosque, a shrine sacred to Moslems and Jews that stands over the tomb of the biblical Abraham.

Palestinians said hundreds of youths fought soldiers with sling shots and stones and hurled some petrol bombs at Israeli soldiers who stayed in parts of Hebron to guard 400 Jewish settlers after Israel handed over most of the city to the PLO in January.
Soldiers fired rubber bullets from behind street corners and broke into houses as Palestinian police struggled to stop the clashes.

Officials at the government-run Alia hospital said two of the wounded were admitted for observation after being hit in the head. Palestinians have died from head wounds caused by rubber-coated bullets.
